misconception_description: Student believes that the body of an if-statement executes repeatedly as long as the condition holds.

solutions.generated_code:
program JumlahRentang
kamus
  n, awal, akhir, i, x, total : integer
algoritma
  input(n, awal, akhir)
  total <- 0
  i <- 1
  if i <= n then
    input(x)
    if i >= awal and i <= akhir then
      total <- total + x
    endif
    i <- i + 1
  endif
  output(total)
endprogram

metadata.modification_notes: The student replaced the for loop with an if-statement, genuinely believing that the if-statement will execute repeatedly as long as the condition (i <= n) remains true. From the student's perspective, the if-statement should keep checking the condition and executing its body (adding list1[i] to sum_range and incrementing i) until i exceeds n, effectively iterating through all indices from m to n. In reality, the if-statement only executes once, so only the element at index m gets added to sum_range, making the function return an incorrect result for any range with more than one element.
